source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading: This Flexential facility is in one of the company national markets confirmed on its own homepage covering Oregon (Portland/Hillsboro), Texas (Dallas, Plano, Richardson), Ohio (West Chester, Cincinnati market), Kentucky (Louisville), Pennsylvania (Allentown, Collegeville, Philadelphia market), Virginia (Richmond), Minnesota (Chaska, Minneapolis market), and Arizona (Phoenix). Flexential was formed from the 2017 merger of ViaWest, founded 1999, and Peak 10, founded 2000, followed by a 2018 rebrand to Flexential. The company reports 40 plus data centers across 18 national markets, 3 million plus square feet of facilities, an 800 million dollar expansion investment, and a planned new campus on 110 acres in Kaufman County near Dallas. This specific state cluster was confirmed as an active Flexential market on the company own site, but no market specific founding, acquisition, or building history distinct from the general ViaWest and Peak 10 company story was located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
Flexential Dallas – Plano publishes 18 MW of IT capacity across 261,400 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 18 MW supports roughly 450 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a more typical enterprise colocation density, the same power budget reaches about 1,800 racks. The arithmetic is an illustration of range, not an operator claim. The floor area works out to approximately 14 square feet per kilowatt at the higher density and 145 square feet per kilowatt at the lower, suggesting the building was sized for mixed or general-purpose colocation rather than GPU-dense AI training pods, though the published specs do not confirm workload mix or rack density in use.

The certification stack qualifies this campus for a specific set of regulated workloads. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 cover financial and operational controls auditing. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data. ITAR restricts eligible tenants to defense and export-controlled technical data. NIST 800-53 aligns the facility with federal security controls. HITRUST addresses healthcare information. SSAE 18 is the attestation standard underlying the SOC reports. Which tenants are present is not published.

Texas has 133 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which only 13 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 389 MW of published IT capacity across the state. Flexential Dallas – Plano's 18 MW ranks ninth among those 13. It holds roughly 4.6 percent of the published Texas total, a mid-tier position in a state where most facilities disclose no capacity figure at all, making the true statewide total unknown.
